# `django/django-unordered-body-content-in-model`

**A model's body follows Django's order**

| | |
|---|---|
| **Pack** | `codelaw-rules-django` (PyPI) |
| **Languages** | Python |
| **Turned on by** | `codelaw:django/recommended` at `warn` |
| **Severity when named without one** | `error` |
| **Options** | none — severity only |
| **Fix** | `suggest` — `codelaw fix --unsafe` applies it; review the diff, it can change behaviour (the field moves above the methods before it, one method a pass, keeping the fields' own order; a comment above the field stays where it was) |
| **Stability** | `preview` — runs only with `preview = true` |
| **Since** | 0.5.0 |
| **Ported from** | `ruff/DJ012` |

## What it checks

Inside a model, fields come before `class Meta`, and both before the methods.

**Why:** Django's style guide orders a model as fields, custom managers, `Meta`, `__str__`, `save`, `get_absolute_url`, then other methods, so every model reads the same way.

## Configuration

Everything below goes in `codelaw.toml` at the repo root. The same keys work as `[tool.codelaw]` in `pyproject.toml` or `"codelaw"` in `package.json` ([SR-CONFIG](../../../records/0110_config.md)).

### Turn it on

**Install the pack** (`codelaw init` does it for the languages it finds):

```bash
pip install codelaw-rules-django
```

**Then extend a preset that turns it on** — `codelaw:django/recommended` sets it to `warn`:

```toml
preview = true                        # pack rules are preview today
extends = ["codelaw:django/recommended"]
```

- **A rule exists only once its pack is loaded** through `extends`; naming it in `[rules]` without that is an unknown rule id (exit 2).
- **Without `preview = true`** the rule is skipped and codelaw warns that it is preview.

### Severity

```toml
[rules]
"django/django-unordered-body-content-in-model" = "warn"    # error | warn | info | off
```

- **`error`** fails the run (exit 1) · **`warn`** fails only with `--max-warnings N` · **`info`** never fails · **`off`** turns it off.
- **Naming it with a severity turns it on** even when no preset does.

### For a group of files

A `[scope.<name>]` gives some files their own setting, applied after `[rules]` — a scope of your own needs `files`:

```toml
[scope.legacy]
files = ["src/legacy/**/*.py"]
rules = { "django/django-unordered-body-content-in-model" = "off" }
```

A scope's `remap` changes whole severities in its files, after everything else: `remap = { error = "warn" }` never fails the run there.

### Warn locally, fail in CI

The `ci` profile runs when `CI` is set; `local` otherwise; `--profile <name>` or `CODELAW_PROFILE` picks one.

```toml
[profile.local.rules]
"django/django-unordered-body-content-in-model" = "warn"

[profile.ci.rules]
"django/django-unordered-body-content-in-model" = "error"
```

### In `pyproject.toml` or `package.json`

```toml
# pyproject.toml
[tool.codelaw.rules]
"django/django-unordered-body-content-in-model" = { severity = "warn" }
```

```json
{
  "codelaw": {
    "rules": {
      "django/django-unordered-body-content-in-model": {"severity": "warn"}
    }
  }
}
```

### Silence one finding

An inline `codelaw-ignore` always needs a reason; `expires=`, `warn_days=` and `by=` date it ([SR-LINTER](../../../records/0106_linter.md) decision 6).

- **Python:** `# codelaw-ignore django/django-unordered-body-content-in-model: <reason>`
- **Dated:** `# codelaw-ignore django/django-unordered-body-content-in-model expires=2026-12-31 by=you@example.com: <reason>`

### Keep today's findings, fail on new ones

```bash
codelaw baseline add --rule django/django-unordered-body-content-in-model --expires 2026-12-31 --reason "<why>"
```

See [SR-BASELINE](../../../records/0104_baseline-and-deprecations.md).

### See what applies

```bash
codelaw explain django/django-unordered-body-content-in-model       # what it wants, why, how to fix
codelaw check --rule django/django-unordered-body-content-in-model  # only this rule
codelaw config --print --for <file>                                 # the resolved setting, and where it came from
```

## How to fix

1. Move the fields to the top of the class and `class Meta` after them, before any method.

## Examples

### Python

#### Don't

```python
class Book(models.Model):
    def __str__(self):
        return self.title

    title = models.CharField(max_length=80)
```

#### Do

```python
class Book(models.Model):
    title = models.CharField(max_length=80)

    def __str__(self):
        return self.title
```

## Differences from the source

Fields and `Meta` after a method are reported; the source also orders managers, `__str__`, `save` and `get_absolute_url` among themselves.
